title: aggregate: a per-measure `filter` compiles to a conditional aggregate in the GROUP BY instead of the in-memory aggregate (epic #33631 R1)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #33631 (SQL performance). Item R1 of the M0 ranked list (#33633): https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889544281 (corrected 6889939163). Maintainer's pick (seat decision card, 2026-11-15T06:44Z): 「R1 R7 R12 各一张+测量卡」.

## Today

A per-measure aggregation `filter` forces the in-memory aggregate: every row of the scoped set is fetched into the app (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` ~1341, ~1392).

## Measured (`aggregate_measure_filter`, p50)

SQLite 383 ms (100k) / 6.2 s (1M); PG 768 ms / 7.3 s (1M).

## Target

Conditional aggregate in the GROUP BY (`sum(case when … end)`; PG `FILTER (WHERE …)` measures the same, ~144 ms): SQLite 5.10 s → 0.53 s, PG 5.09 s → 0.14 s (10x–36x). A driver-sql capability flag decides; analytics measures (A3) consume it.

## Business reason

Any dashboard measure with its own filter ("won amount", "open count") fetches the whole set into the app; at 1M rows a single tile takes 6–7 s.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area A4 (engine + driver-sql), A3 consumer; next account; size M.

## Epic rules

- Name the SQL shape produced and give before/after on the M0 bench (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf`, PR #33662).
- Security never regresses: read scope and tenant wall stay in the pushed-down statement, with a parity test against today's path.
- A non-SQL driver keeps an in-process path it already has or refuses with a stable code (epic #33631 rules; #33626 rulings).
